counterfactual_missing_items: No Brucella-specific serology or culture identification is supplied
The organism is reported only as a Gram-negative bacillus, not specifically as Brucella species
No response to brucellosis-specific therapy is described
decisive_items: He reported touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand about 1 month earlier
On hospital day 6, blood cultures grew a Gram-negative bacillus
Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10
response.rationale: R2 is the only candidate that links the highly specific exposure to unpasteurized sheep material with subacute fever, back pain, Gram-negative bacteremia, and spinal/epidural infection; this is the classic brucellosis syndrome. R1 is a strong runner-up because it names the emergent epidural complication and cord compression, but it lacks the upstream causative exposure that explains why the patient developed infection. R4 and C1 describe local vertebral imaging findings, R5 is a nonspecific microbiologic observation, and R7 has no diagnostic disc-space evidence.

rejected.why: Describes the vertebral osteomyelitis component but not the underlying etiologic agent and lacks the complication/cord evidence.
Gram-negative bacillus infection is too nonspecific and only reports the culture result rather than a complete clinical diagnosis.
Back pain and tenderness are nonspecific; no discriminating disc-space or discitis-specific finding is supplied.
Append-only completion of R4, adding only the T9 anatomy without an independent cause or broader syndrome.
